text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert — sustained 5xx-rate spike (>=12%) on dedicated-us-east-3 pool serving Stellarix. Paging oncall.
Amanda: oncall taking. I see increased 5xx in autoscaler logs and some OOM kill signals on GPU nodes.
Ricardo: thanks. can you snapshot the pool and attach node IDs? I'll start immediate routing fallback to hosted tier for affected account.
Amanda: node IDs: gpu-us-e3-42, gpu-us-e3-43, gpu-us-e3-47. attaching recent container logs snippet.
Amanda: ```
2026-03-17T09:21:03Z engine:oom-kill pid=4321 model-server
2026-03-17T09:21:08Z runtime:error evicting kv cache mem=91% -> kill
2026-03-17T09:21:12Z proxy:502 upstream-reset code=OOM
```
Priya: if we failover to hosted for Stellarix, we need a tailored customer notice and routing plan. Jan, can support own the customer comms and contact list?
Jan (support): I have Stellarix primary contacts: e.contact@stellarix.com, ops-esc@stellarix.com, and their CSM Liaison (lia@stellarix.com). I'll prepare a targeted note once we agree wording.
Kai (oncall): Amanda — please put affected model versions on fallback list and route new requests to hosted-llm-4 for that tenant only. Update routing policy to preserve latency SLOs.
Amanda: applied routing override: tenant=stellarix -> hosted-llm-4, ttl=30m, reason=dedicated-pool-5xx. Keeping read-only KV cache until mem stabilizes.
Ricardo: starting canary drain of gpu-us-e3-43 then 42. scaling policy bump to add two standby GPUs in the pool to investigate.
Priya: draft customer-facing status (please edit):
Priya: "Stellarix — We're experiencing degraded inference availability for some requests served from your dedicated GPU pool (us-east-3). We've routed new traffic to a hot-hosted fallback to maintain availability while we remediate. You may see increased latency on a subset of requests during the transition. No data loss is expected. ETA for full restore: 60–90 minutes. We'll update within 30 minutes or when we have a mitigation. — Redwood Inference Ops"
Jan (support): that reads well. Suggest adding a dedicated line for contact routing: "For urgent impacts, reply to this thread or email ops-esc@stellarix.com and we'll escalate immediately."
Amanda: ops update: OOM traces on node 47 show tensor cache growth tied to a specific model variant (v2-int8). I'm killing the suspect pods and will redeploy with reduced kv-cache-size.
Ricardo: good. please push rollback to v2-int7 on affected nodes if pod restarts don't stabilize within 10m.
Amanda: done — killed pods on 47, redeploying v2-int7 with kv_cache_limit=256MB.
Kai (oncall): monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 12.3% -> 3.1% after routing override + redeploy. continuing to watch.
Priya: Jan, please send the customer note now with subject: "Stellarix — Temporary routing to hosted fallback (Mar 17)" and paste the draft. Mark as high-touch.
Jan (support): sent to contacts and Cc'd CSM. I included the diagnostic summary and a link to the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1779991234
incident-bot: Incident updated: priority=SEV2 -> mitigated (partial). Next update window: +30m. Incident owner: Amanda.
Amanda: leaving a quick runbook step for postmortem: collect heap snapshots from gpu-us-e3-42/43/47, include model version metrics, and export autoscaler logs for the 2-hour window around spike.
Ricardo: once stable, we'll schedule a maintenance window to repro with synthetic load and validate kv_cache_limit changes across staging.
Priya: thanks team. I'll draft the public status page blurb after final confirmation. Good work on the handoff and targeted routing.
Jan (support): will keep Stellarix updated and will reopen comms thread if any regression.
Amanda: closing oncall here; handing back to Ricardo for infra follow-ups. Amanda out.
Ricardo: taking infra follow-ups. I'll update last_message_ts when we close the incident."
